'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[Islamic State–Taliban conflict]]
***[[Taliban]] spokesperson [[Suhail Shaheen]] rules out cooperation with the [[United States]] to fight the [[insurgency]] of [[Islamic State – Khorasan Province|IS–K]] in [[Afghanistan]], saying that the Taliban "will be able to tackle [[Islamic State|Daesh]] independently". [https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4310632 (''Taiwan News'')]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**At least 20 people are killed as gunmen [[mass shooting|open fire]] at a market and torch cars in [[Sokoto]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/10/gunmen-raid-nigeria-market-kill-at-least-20-people (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Mali War]]
**A [[Colombians|Colombian]] [[Roman Catholic nun]] who had been [[kidnap]]ped in [[Mali]] near [[Burkina Faso–Mali border|the border]] with [[Burkina Faso]] in 2017 by the [[Macina Liberation Front]] is freed. The nun is photographed with [[President of Mali|Malian President]] [[Assimi Goïta]] as the [[government of Mali|government]] refuses to state if any [[ransom]] was paid for her release. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/colombian-nun-held-hostage-mali-since-2017-has-been-freed-presidency-says-2021-10-09/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Cumbre Vieja eruption]]
**The north face of the volcano collapses, generating three new lava flows. No new evacuations have been ordered as authorities call for calm. [https://elpais.com/sociedad/2021-10-09/la-cara-norte-del-volcan-de-la-palma-se-derrumba-de-manera-parcial-y-arrasa-nuevas-construcciones.html (''El País'')]
*[[Russia]]n authorities say that 29 people have died in [[Orenburg Oblast]] during the past week due to [[alcohol poisoning]], after drinking a beverage mixed with [[methanol]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/alcohol-poisoning-leaves-26-dead-russia-2021-10-09/ (Reuters)]
*The Deir Ammar and Zahrani [[power station]]s shut down in [[Lebanon]] after running out of diesel fuel, leaving the entire country without electricity. According to a government official, power is not expected to be restored for several days. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-58856914 (BBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/9/fuel-shortage-forces-shutdown-main-lebanese-power-plants (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria]]
****[[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 1,965 new cases and five deaths from COVID-19, which is the highest daily total of new [[COVID-19]] cases in any [[States and territories of Australia|Australian state]] or territory. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-10-09/victoria-covid-wrap-october-9/100526504 (ABC News Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
***[[Russia]] reports a record 968 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 215,453. [https://apnews.com/article/coronavirus-pandemic-moscow-europe-russia-health-cac40f6eae4fbee9fa53bc36ee2eb653 (AP)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
***[[Singapore]] reports a record 3,703 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 124,157. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/health/11-people-aged-between-56-and-90-die-of-covid-19-3703-new-infections-in-spore (''The Straits Times'')]
**[[Mental health during the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***A study conducted by researchers from the [[University of Queensland]] concludes that the COVID-19 pandemic led to a significant increase in diagnoses of [[generalized anxiety disorder]] and [[major depressive disorder]] worldwide in [[2020]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/oct/08/covid-crisis-dramatically-worsened-global-mental-health-study-finds (''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Afghanistan–United States relations]]
**The [[U.S. State Department]] confirms that the first face-to-face meetings with high representatives of the Taliban since the [[Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan (2020–2021)|departure]] of [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. troops]] from Afghanistan, will begin today in [[Doha]], [[Qatar]]. A spokesperson for the State Department says that the U.S. will pressure the Taliban to "respect the rights of all Afghans, including women and girls" and form an inclusive [[government of Afghanistan|government]]. The spokesperson also clarifies that this is not a recognition of the Taliban government by the U.S., saying that the Taliban will have to earn recognition by its actions. [https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20211009-us-to-hold-first-in-person-talks-with-taliban-since-afghan-withdrawal (France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Memorandum of understanding between Argentina and Iran]]
**Families of the victims of the 1994 [[AMIA bombing]] in [[Buenos Aires]] announce that they will appeal the ruling which acquitted former [[President of Argentina|president]] [[Cristina Fernández de Kirchner]] of any wrongdoing. The memorandum aimed to make [[Iran]] cooperate in the investigation at the time that [[Argentina]] issued [[red notice]]s against Iranian officials through [[Interpol]]. [[Argentina-Iran relations|Relations between Argentina and Iran]] have been strained, with a recent condemnation by Argentina of the new [[cabinet of Argentina|cabinet]] of [[Ebrahim Raisi]]. [https://en.mercopress.com/2021/10/09/argentina-relatives-of-amia-bombing-victims-to-appeal-court-ruling-dismissing-charges-against-cfk (MercoPress)]
*[[Central American migrant caravans]]
**[[Policía Nacional Civil (Guatemala)|Guatemalan police]] recover 126 [[Immigration to the United States|United States-bound]] [[Haitian diaspora|Haitian]], [[Nepalis|Nepali]], and [[Non-resident Indian and person of Indian origin|Indian migrants]] trapped inside an abandoned [[shipping container]] near [[Nueva Concepción, Escuintla]], [[Guatemala]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/guatemala-police-find-126-migrants-in-shipping-container (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]
*In [[Rome]], [[Italy]], demonstrators protesting against the country's COVID-19 restrictions, notably the extension of the [[Immunity passport#COVID-19|Green Pass]], clash with police, and the demonstrations turn into riots. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/9/clashes-break-out-in-rome-amid-anger-over-covid-19-green-pass (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Czech legislative election]]
**The opposition [[Spolu (Czech Republic)|SPOLU]] party calls for the formation of a new [[government of the Czech Republic|government]] in view of the poor electoral result of [[Prime Minister of the Czech Republic|prime minister]] [[Andrej Babiš]]' [[ANO (political party)|ANO 2011]] party. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/czechs-vote-final-day-election-pm-babis-seeks-cling-power-2021-10-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[Kurz corruption probe]]
**[[Chancellor of Austria|Austrian Chancellor]] [[Sebastian Kurz]] [[resign]]s amid a [[corruption]] inquiry against him, although he continues to deny any wrongdoing. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-58856796 (BBC News)]
